reason: The cited evidence shows that nitriding at 750–850 °C increases hardness but that adding texturing at these temperatures actually increases wear volume (E1, E2), directly contradicting the predicted 50% wear reduction. The hardness increase is supported qualitatively but the specific 200% value is not evidenced, and the compressive stress mechanism is supported only for fatigue, not wear (E3).
premises: Plasma nitriding at 750 °C for 4 h in NH3:N2 (1:2) forms a continuous hard Ti–N compound layer on Ti–6Al–4V
The nitride layer increases surface hardness by over 200% (e.g., from ~350 HV to >1000 HV)
Laser surface texturing after nitriding reduces wear rate by ~50% under high-load dry sliding
Nitriding induces compressive residual stresses that inhibit crack initiation and dislocation motion
Laser texturing reduces contact area, traps debris, and distributes contact stresses to lower friction and wear
